find: ``a matter of grace, and not on compulsion''
replace: ``a matter of grace, though not upon compulsion''
reason: Iredell (quoting Blackstone) writes that the Chancellor will 'administer right, as a matter of grace, though not upon compulsion.' The brief altered the wording inside quotation marks.

find: Georgia likewise sued South Carolina citizens in the Supreme Court
replace: Georgia likewise sued Samuel Brailsford (a British subject) and his South Carolina partners in the Supreme Court
reason: In Georgia v. Brailsford the defendants were Brailsford, a British subject, and Powell and Hopton, who were citizens of South Carolina; 'South Carolina citizens' is only partly accurate (reviewer concern).
source: https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/84683/georgia-v-brailsford/ (3 U.S. (3 Dall.) 1 (1794): 'Hopton & Powell (who were citizens of South-Carolina)'; debts of 'Brailsford, Powell & Hopton')

find: Georgia was simultaneously suing South Carolina citizens as a plaintiff
replace: Georgia was simultaneously suing a British creditor and his South Carolina partners as a plaintiff
reason: Same issue in the Reasoning section: the Brailsford defendants were a British subject (Brailsford) and two South Carolina citizens (Powell and Hopton).
